2 JUDGMENT :
[PER : SHYAM C. CHANDAK, J.] :-
1) Present Appeal filed under Section 11 of The Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (In Financial Establishments) Act, 1999 P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc (for short 'the MPID Act') impugned the Order dated 10th February 2023, passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune whereby the learned Judge rejected the Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.177 of 2021 (for short 'the Application'), filed under Section 156(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
seeking for direction to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune to register FIR and commence investigation for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 409, 420 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the MPID Act, against Respondent Nos.2 to 6, who were arraigned as accused Nos.1 to 5 in the said Application.
1.1) Hereinafter, the parties are being referred to by their original status in the Application i.e.,
Appellants as 'Complainants' and Respondent Nos.2 to 6 as 'Accused'.
2) Heard Mr. Nashikkar, Advocate for Appellants, Mrs. Takalkar, learned APP for Respondent No.1-State and Mr. Rajiv Chavan, learned Senior Advocate for Respondent Nos.2 to 6.
Perused entire record.

3) The Complainants had filed the Criminal Application No.177 of 2021 wherein it was stated that,
Accused no.1-M/s.Bhimashankar Developers has been doing the business of development of real estate, construction and other allied activities.
Accused Nos.2 to 5 are the partners of accused no.1.

In the month of May 2017, the accused persons told the Complainants that, they have floated a real estate scheme i.e., 'Buy Back Scheme' in respect of a land bearing Gat No.372, Amberwadi,
Khandala, P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc Satara.
That, money deposited in the said scheme will be multiplied into seven to eight times and it will be returned after two years.
In the alternative, the Complainants will have an option to retain certain plots in the said land, instead of taking back the deposited money, but upon payment of certain amount.
Trusting the said representations made by the accused, the Complainants agreed to deposit their money in that scheme.

3.1) Accordingly, MoU dated 20th May, 2017 was entered into between the parties containing the details of the deposited amount, the land, the assured compensation/interest and the terms and conditions.

Thereafter, the Complainants invested Rs.2,69,700/- each by a cheque dated 03rd June, 2017 with the accused persons totaling to Rs.5,39,500/- on a promise from the accused that, they would return the said amount along with the compensation/interest of Rs.41,45,594/- in a phased manner by post dated cheques, upon the expiration of 24 months.

Alternatively, the Complainants will have an option of retaining Plot Nos. 36 and 37, admeasuring 450.15 sq. mtrs,
upon additional payment of Rs.4,28,200/- at the time of handing over possession of the said plots.
At the time of execution of the said MoU, the accused persons issued total 24 month-wise post dated cheques, each of Rs.1,72,733/-, for the period from 20 th May, 2019 to 20th April, 2020.

sentences.text: It is alleged that, in the month of May 2019, the Complainants visited the said plots' location and found that, there was no development P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc nor necessary Government sanction/permissions were taken by the accused persons.
The Complainants confronted the accused persons with the said fact.
Further, they requested the accused to cancel the said plots and pay the assured compensation of Rs.41,45,594/-.
The accused persons agreed for that.
Therefore, the Complainants insisted that, they would deposit the aforesaid cheques for encashment to realize the compensation including the principle amount.
However, the accused persons showed their inability to pay the said amount on the pretext that, they are going through financial crisis.
Therefore, the Complainants did not deposit the cheques.
3.3) It is alleged that, thereafter, the Complainants followed up with the accused persons on numerous occasions and demanded the deposited amount along with the compensation/interest.
Therefore, from August 2019, the accused persons started to repay the installments.

Till January, 2020 the accused persons paid total Rs.4,69,450/- only and avoided to pay the balance amount as per the MoU. Thereafter, the Complainants learn that, the accused persons siphoned the funds of accused no.1 to other shell entities and sister companies.

Thus, the accused persons deceived the Complainants and dishonestly induced them to deposit their money by floating nonviable development scheme in respect of the said land but without any intention to return the deposited money along with the promised compensation/interest.

Hence, the Complainants sent a written complaint by post to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune, Commissioner of P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc Police, Pune,
Deputy Commissioner of Police, Pune, EOW and Cyber Cell, Pune on 11th May, 2021.
However, the police have not done any investigation in the matter.
Consequently, the Applicant filed the Criminal Miscellaneous Application No.177 of 2021.

4) After considering the Application and submissions made by the Advocate for the Complainants,
the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune noted that, in the month of August, 2019 the accused persons initiated to pay the compensation in installments and till January, 2020 they paid total Rs.4,69,750/- to the Complainants.
Thus, in the month of August 2019 itself, the Complainants knew that, the accused persons were not in a position to repay the invested amount.
However, the Complainants persuaded with the accused persons for refund of their money.
Thereafter, only the Complainants sent their complaint to Shivaji Nagar Police Station, Pune.
In this background, the learned Judge held that, the transaction in question was of civil nature.
This fact was within the knowledge of the Complainants.
Therefore, till 10th May 2021, the Complainants have not approached the police nor to the Court.
Hence, the learned Judge persuaded to reject the Application.
Hence, Appeal.
5) Mr. Nashikkar, Advocate for the Appellants submitted that, the accused persons had floated a completely nonviable scheme of investment and returns.
This conduct itself manifests that, since inception there was intention on the part of the accused to cheat the Complainants.

After P.H.
Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc accepting the said deposit, the accused persons siphoned that amount to shell entities/sister companies.
Thus, this is a clear case of cheating and misappropriation.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, it is evident that, the amount invested by the Complainants was a 'Deposit' and the accused persons were falling in the definition of 'Financial Establishments' as defined under Section 2 (c) and 2 (d) of the MPID Act.

However, the learned Judge completely ignored the above and erroneously held that, the Mitesh Prakash Jain (Huf) Through Its ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5866576/
4 transaction in question is of civil nature.
Therefore, the impugned Order is not sustainable in law and is liable to be quashed.
To buttress his submissions, the learned Advocate placed his reliance on following decisions.
We have carefully considered the same.

i) State of Maharashtra vs. 63 Moons Technologies, (2024) SCC OnLine SC 223,
ii) Rajiv Ramanlal Shah vs. Senior Inspector of Police Criminal Writ Petition No.1224 of 2001 dtd.
24/01/2002 iii) S. W. Palnitkar vs. State of Bihar, (2002) 1 SCC 241 iv) Dr. Lakhsman vs. State of Karnataka, (2019) 9 SCC 677 v) Manohar Bhimraoji Mahalle vs. State of Maharashtra, 2020 SCC Online Bom. 368 vi) Ajay vs. State of Maharashtra, Criminal Writ Petition No.108 of 2021 dated 21/10/2022 5.1)
Learned APP submitted that, considering the facts and circumstances of the case necessary Order may be passed.

6) In contrast, Mr. Rajiv Chavan, learned Senior Advocate for the  P.H. Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc Respondent Nos.2 to 6 submitted that, even though, the Complainants alleged that, after expiry of the two years period they cancelled the MoU and requested for the compensation/interest amount,
notice to that effect was not issued by the Complainants.
The Complainants did not avail the option of purchasing the proposed plots by paying balance consideration.
Majority of the principal amount was already returned to the Complainants by the accused.
Considering these facts and the delay in filing the said Application, the learned Judge has rightly held that, this is purely a case of civil nature.
Hence, the rejection of the Application cannot be questioned by way of this Appeal.
7) Considering the record and the rival submissions, it is noticed that, out of the principal amount of Rs.5,39,500/-, the accused have already returned total Rs.4,69,750/- to the Complainants.
This fact indicates that, the Complainants did not avail the option of purchasing the plots by paying the balance consideration.
The Complainants have not deposited the cheques drawn by the accused.
From the MoU it is evident that, the prospective returns were highly excessive.
In the said Application itself the Complainants have stated that, the representations made by the accused persons were malicious.
Thus, since inception the Complainants knew the aforesaid facts.

Yet, the Mitesh Prakash Jain (Huf) Through Its ... vs State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5866576/

Therefore, it cannot be said that, the accused persons deceived the Complainants and dishonestly induced them to enter P.H.
Jayani 72 APEAL436.2023.doc.doc into the said MoU.

In fact, on careful reading of the MoU it seems that, the Complainants entered into the said transaction on their own, willingly and after understanding its minute details only to earn an exorbitant interest but knowingly taking risk of their money.
Therefore, the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Pune has rightly held that, the subject dispute is of civil nature.
8) In so far as the reported decisions cited by the Advocate for Complainants are concerned, the facts of the said cases and the case in hand are distinct and therefore those are of no help to him.
8.1) In view thereof, we find no illegality in the impugned Order.
As a result, the Appeal is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
